newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Jollibee lowers 97 net growth target.
newsitem.headline: Jollibee lowers 97 net growth target.

text.p: The Philippines' fastfood leader, Jollibee Foods Corp, said on Monday it now expects net income to grow by 10 percent rather than the 20 percent originally projected.

"We will downgrade our net income projection because our operating cost relative to marketing and labour costs were not matched by a price increase," Jollibee vice-president for finance Raffy dela Rosa told Reuters by phone.
Asked whether the company will raise prices, Dela Rosa said: "There are no definite plans to increase prices as of today."
Jollibee earlier reported that its net profit in 1996 reached 603 million pesos.
Dela Rosa said company expenses rose due to advertising and marketing costs and a minimum wage increase early in the year.
But the company would not change its original forecast of a 25 percent rise in gross revenues for the year, he said.
"Our sales have been strong and are beyond expectations," the official said. He did not elaborate.
He said Jollibee would release first six months earnings results on July 31 but declined to give details.

This month's de facto devaluation of the peso, Dela Rosa said, would mean a 43 million peso one-time loss for the company to be booked by the third quarter, if the peso-dollar rate settles at 28 pesos.
He said the loss would come from a $28 million loan.
Dela Rosa added the company had postponed plans to issue new shares to September from the original May schedule due to market conditions.
The firm earlier said it planned to raise 1.5 billion pesos by issuing new shares or warrants, or offering a convertible bond.
